source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    When SUT occur error/warning event, the fault LED will bright up.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: The fault LED will response the system fault status.

original_test_intent: Verify that the physical fault LED for a specified CPU node illuminates or otherwise changes in accordance with a defined CPU-node error or warning state.
original_method: Create or observe an approved CPU-node error/warning event, visually record the mapped node fault LED, correlate it with fault telemetry, and verify recovery. The source does not state which event or how to produce it.
manual_activity: After unblocking, a qualified operator must visually observe the exact CPU-node LED. Before that, no person or agent should invent a CPU fault event merely to make the LED respond.
required_inputs: Exact CPU node/topology and physical LED mapping
Defined warning/fault type, severity and owner-approved bounded stimulus
Expected LED state and response/clear timing for that event
Maintenance impact, OOB monitoring, stop criteria and tested recovery procedure
safety_requirements: Do not offline, reset, overheat, electrically fault or power-cycle a CPU/node using guessed methods.
Do not run any injector until blast radius, workload evacuation, expected event and recovery are approved.
Require visual LED evidence plus event telemetry; neither can substitute for the other.
Stop on unexpected severity, system instability, wrong-node response or OOB loss; preserve logs and never auto-retry.
agent_execution_scope: While blocked, inventory the proposed node/LED mapping and prepare read-only baseline/evidence collection only.
After approval, supervise only the explicitly bounded stimulus and correlate event, LED observation and recovery records.
Do not claim the physical observation or formal verdict.
engineer_actions: Define and approve a safe CPU-node event and recovery specific to this platform.
Provide the LED response table and qualified visual operator.
Authorize execution and decide the result after complete recovery evidence.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: No executable command was supplied, but its generic LED-table description is not a runnable or safe method and omits the essential fault stimulus.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No command is recommended while blocked. Retain any future owner-approved platform fault-injection procedure verbatim with version, scope and recovery; do not invent a generic CPU injector.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The error/warning-triggered LED intent and both five-minute fields are retained, although the source supplies no usable stimulus parameters.

modernized_recommendation.status: NO SAFE MODERNIZATION UNTIL STIMULUS IS DEFINED
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: First bind one documented platform-supported CPU warning/fault to the exact node LED state and a tested clear/recovery path; only then create a synchronized event/visual evidence plan.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Undetermined until CPU-node and platform fault mechanism are supplied.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS, BMC, CPLD, CPU and injector/tool versions after selection.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Owner platform fault-injection and LED specifications are required; no external generic command is asserted.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds the missing safe stimulus, expected event and recovery gates without changing the visual acceptance target.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Cannot be assessed until the selected event is mapped to the intended CPU-node fault class.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Node map, event, LED table, timing and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Different injectors exercise different RAS paths; a convenient software error may not drive the hardware LED.

project_override_considerations: A project may select a supported CPU RAS injection or use a naturally occurring controlled warning, but it must document the exact covered path. Merely supplying a package or parameter is insufficient here because the necessary operation semantics are undefined.
expected_evidence: Approved node/LED map and fault-state table
Documented bounded stimulus, impact, response timeout and recovery authorization
Timestamped stimulus/event logs and operator visual evidence of the mapped LED
Pre/during/post BMC/host/SEL/RAS health and proven service recovery

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The procedure and criterion both call for an LED response to a system fault. The problem is missing essential operational semantics, not contradictory source statements.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The case cannot be executed safely or evaluated because no CPU node, fault/warning stimulus, LED response mapping, timeout or recovery method is defined. Guessing any of these could disrupt or damage the SUT.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Reject its unsupported generic color table and record that visual limitation alone is not the decisive blocker; the undefined fault operation is.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agree with BLOCKED and its requirement for a node-specific bounded stimulus and recovery.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Makes the blocking semantics explicit while preserving a future manual visual step after safe unblocking.

review_improvement: Separates an intrinsically manual LED observation from the currently unsafe, undefined fault-generation prerequisite and avoids fabricating a RAS command.
independent_technical_reasoning: Unlike passive heartbeat observation, this case depends on a causal error/warning condition. CPU RAS injection paths vary in severity and may reset or offline the node, while some may never drive this LED. Without the event-to-indicator mapping and recovery, neither automation capability nor a safe manual plan exists, so BLOCKED is justified.
